summary: Hot-turn prefetch fanout causes cache missstorm and intermittent request timeouts for replayed conversational turns
description:
Issue summary:
Noteable Analytics reported intermittent p99/p999 latency spikes and increased 504s when they replay identical conversational turns at high parallel fanout. Problem appears only on their dedicated pool in us-east-1 and corresponds to bursts of KV prefix-cache misses.

Impact:
- Customer seeing 5-15% of generation requests time out during replay-heavy workloads (their QA harness replays the same turn across 200 concurrent sessions).
- Visible increase in per-request token cost due to repeated full-context re-evaluation after cache misses.
- Business impact: page templates and chat replays failing during demos; escalated to CS.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool (d3.large-gpu cluster) in us-east-1
- Serving runtime version: 2.8.1
- KV cache service: kv-prefetch v1.7 (internal build)
- Autoscaler version: autoscale-3.2

Steps to reproduce (customer supplied):
1. Create 200 parallel websocket streams to /v1/chat/stream with the same conversation turn (same prefix) replayed across sessions.
2. Ensure session affinity is disabled on the client (they use ephemeral session ids).
3. Observe generation latency and count 504 responses over a 10-minute run.

Observed logs / metrics (samples):
- p99 generation latency jump from ~220ms -> ~1.9s during burst windows.
- 504 count: 0.8% baseline -> 6.3% during spike window.
- KVCACHE-prefetch miss rate: 2% -> 48% on affected shard set.
- Metric spike correlated with short-lived node churn events reported by autoscaler (node retire/replace events within the same minute).

Initial investigation notes:
- Support reproduced a scaled-down version in staging using the customer's harness; confirmed miss amplification when many parallel replays target the same prefix.
- Cache telemetry shows an amplification pattern where a single hot prefix causes N concurrent prefetch requests to the backing store when prefetch deduplication fails.
- Deduplication failure seems to align with requests that lost session-affinity and re-routed to a shard that had an in-flight invalidation token.
- Autoscaler churn made the effect worse: when a node is removed and shards migrate, the prefetch dedupe map briefly contains concurrent keys with different ephemeral shard tokens, allowing duplicate prefetches to proceed.

Hypothesis:
- The prefetch deduplication key includes a shard-instance token that changes on migration. Rapid parallel replays with ephemeral session ids + node churn produce differing dedupe keys for the same logical prefix, causing a "missstorm" where many backends simultaneously fetch the same prefix. This overwhelms the backing store and increases end-to-end latency, and some requests time out.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Support suggested customer enable consistent session-affinity in their dedicated pool (customer accepted and tested). Results: immediate reduction in missstorm amplitude but did not fully eliminate spikes during autoscaler churn.
- Applied conservative rate-limiting on prefetch concurrency at the edge (config change rolled to affected nodes) to bound fanout from 200->16 concurrent prefetches. This reduced 504s to ~1.6% for the next test window.

Engineering actions / root cause fix plan:
- Patch prefetch dedupe: move dedupe key away from ephemeral shard-instance token to stable shard-id + prefix hash (PR linked). Patch backported to 2.8.x.
- Improve migration handshake: add short grace window where migrating shards forward in-flight prefetch dedupe records to target to avoid duplicate fetches.
- Add automated test that simulates node migration + high-fanout replay to prevent regressions.
- Rollout plan: canary patch to 10% of dedicated pools in us-east-1 -> monitor kv-prefetch miss rate and 504s for 48 hours -> full rollout.

Resolution notes (work in progress):
- Patch merged to main and cherry-picked to release-2.8 (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8942).
- Canary scheduled 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC for the affected cluster.
- Customer advised to keep session-affinity enabled until full rollout completes.

Follow-up items:
- Postmortem doc to be created after full verification (owner: Ethan Blake).
- Add observability metric: dedupe-duplicate-prefetch-count per shard.
- Update runbook for dedicated customers to recommend session-affinity for replay-heavy workloads.

workaround: Enable session-affinity for the dedicated pool; limit client parallel replays to <50 concurrent streams; temporary prefetch concurrency cap applied by Support.
next_steps: Monitor canary for 48 hours; if stable, promote patch to all dedicated pools in us-east-1 and then global. Complete postmortem and add dedupe metrics to dashboards.
